newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki up, trims gains as active Nokia retreats.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki up, trims gains as active Nokia retreats.

text.p: Shares ended a volatile session off highs with focus on Nokia which retreated from earlier strong gains that followed rumours that it would merge with its rival Ericsson, brokers said.
Analysts said the rumours were ill-informed but some added there were also fundamental grounds for Nokia's share to rise.

The dollar's strength and early gains in U.S. treasuries following a decline in the U.S. trade deficit in October helped shares in the afternoon, leaving scope for further gains on Friday if bonds stayed strong.
Options and futures expiry boosted trading, brokers said.
Nokia closed up 5.00 at 260.50 after hitting a 265 markka intra-session peak. Volume was a massive 450 million markka.
"The Finnish stock market will rise on any kind of rumours no matter how unrealistic," one broker said referring to the market's merger talk.
Forestries were supported by the dollar and the sector's gains in the U.S. but trade was thin except for UPM-Kymmene which closed flat at 94.00 after almost 60 million markka trade.
Amer see-sawed but ended in positive territory after opening weak on saying that restructuring of the Wilson golf business would take time. It closed at 90.50, up 0.80.
